title: GHARP: Real-Time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-Scale Reconstruction Prior
gist: Apple researchers present GHARP (ACCV, October 2026), a two-stage method for animating 3D Gaussian human heads in real time from a few images. An expensive offline identity stage is paired with a lightweight runtime animation network built for mobile devices. A body alignment network removes blur and flicker in body regions, and the method reports state-of-the-art quality on Ava-256 while running up to 13x faster with 8x fewer Gaussians.

insights.claim: GHARP splits head-avatar animation into two parts. An identity stage builds the subject's geometry and appearance offline, and it can be expensive. An animation stage then predicts expression-dependent residuals at runtime with a lightweight network optimized for mobile devices.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The heavy compute happens once, ahead of time, while the per-frame work fits on a phone. That points to Apple running real-time photoreal avatars on-device, for example for FaceTime or Vision Pro-style personas.
insights.quote: the identity stage can be expensive while the animation stage runs a lightweight network, optimized for mobile devices

insights.claim: GHARP animates inside the semantically structured latent space of a pretrained reconstruction model, where expression changes stay spatially contained. This makes residual prediction efficient and lets multiple input views be fused into a compact, fixed-size canonical Gaussian representation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Reusing a large reconstruction prior, here the earlier HeadsUp work, as the backbone for animation shows Apple building a stacked avatar pipeline rather than one-off models.
insights.quote: expression changes remain spatially contained, making residual prediction efficient

insights.claim: All expression-driven avatar methods share a problem: expression codes describe only the face, so body pose and clothing position are left out. The animation network then averages over conflicting body appearances, which produces blur and temporal flicker.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Identifies a quality bottleneck shared by the whole field of avatar methods, not just this one, which helps when judging how believable competing telepresence avatars will look.
insights.quote: expression codes describe only the face and thus omit body pose and clothing position

insights.claim: GHARP adds a body alignment network that aligns the person's body in the target image with the input reference images. This removes the ambiguity from the training signal that causes blur and flicker.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A targeted fix for the clear visual artifacts in body regions that make current avatars look fake.

insights.claim: GHARP reports state-of-the-art quality on the Ava-256 benchmark while running up to 13x faster on an A100 GPU and using 8x fewer Gaussians than prior methods.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude gain in efficiency is what moves photoreal avatars from datacenter GPUs to edge devices.
